For each operating scenario, provide load flow results on the diagram or in the report. Show or describe the loading factors and assumptions used in each operating mode.
3.2.5 Fault Current Study
Use the results of the load flow study to perform the fault current study in accordance with IEEE 3002.3. Provide balanced three-phase fault, bolted line-to-line fault, and single line-to-ground fault current values at each voltage transformation point and at each power distribution bus. For each location, show in tabular form on the diagram or in the report the maximum and minimum available fault currents of all modes of operation for that location.
Where the available fault current at the source bus is not available, describe how the fault contribution from the source bus was determined and why this method is reasonable for the study.
3.2.6 System Coordination Study
Use the results of the load flow study and fault current study. For normal modes of operation, demonstrate that selectivity has been obtained between the devices within the scope of the project. Demonstrate the equipment, machines, and conductors are protected from damage from overloads and fault conditions. Include a description of the coordination of the protective devices in this project. Provide a written narrative describing which devices may operate in the event of a fault at each bus; the logic used to arrive at device ratings and settings; situations where system coordination is not achievable due to device limitations; coordination between upstream and downstream devices; and relay settings. Provide recommendations to improve or enhance system reliability, and detail where such changes would involve additions or modifications to the contract and cost damages (addition or reduction). Provide composite coordination plots on a log-log scale. Where recommendations are provided to improve or enhance system reliability, provide separate coordination plots on log-log scale showing the system coordination before and after the implementation of the recommendations. Utilize the data from the fault current study to determine the worst case incident energy per IEEE 1584, IEEE C2, and OSHA 29 CFR 1910.269 Appendix E. Use identified modes of operation to determine the worst case arc flash energy. If not included in another study, include a description of the devices and device settings for the operating modes that provided the highest arc flash energy. 1.9.1 System Description
The interior distribution system consists of the 480Y/277 V and 208Y/120 V feeders, raceways, wiring devices, dry-type transformers T-1A (112.5 kVA), T-2A (75 kVA), T-C1 (45 kVA, K-13 rated) and T-E1 (45 kVA), panelboards HM1, H1A, H2A, HE1, LP1A, LP2A, LC1 and LE1, surge protective devices at MSB and LC1, and the grounding and bonding system.
1.9.2 Conductors and Raceways
Provide copper conductors throughout. Feeder insulation is XHHW-2 and branch-circuit insulation is THHN/THWN-2. Metal-clad and armored cable are not permitted.
Raceways are EMT where concealed and above ceilings, rigid metal conduit where exposed below 8 feet in mechanical and electrical rooms and on building exteriors, and PVC Schedule 40 underground and in slabs with RMC or PVC-coated RMC elbows and risers. Liquidtight flexible metal conduit is limited to final connections to vibrating equipment and must not exceed 6 feet. ENT, LFNC and surface nonmetallic raceway are not permitted.
1.9.3 Voltage Drop and Raceway Fill
Voltage drop must not exceed 3 percent for feeders and service conductors and 3 percent for branch circuits, with not more than 5 percent total from the point of Government ownership to the furthest outlet. Voltage drop of any feeder of the emergency system must not exceed 2 percent. Calculate feeder voltage drop over the one-way routed length of the feeder.
Where more than two conductors are installed in one raceway, the sum of the overall conductor areas must not exceed 40 percent of the interior cross-sectional area of the raceway. Install each parallel conductor set in its own raceway.
1.9.4 Grounding
The building grounding electrode system resistance must not exceed 10 ohms, measured by the fall-of-potential method. Provide a building ground ring bonded to the grounding electrode system.
1.9.5 Dry-Type Transformers
Dry-type transformers must meet the efficiency levels of 10 CFR 431.196(a)(3) that apply to units manufactured on or after April 23, 2029, regardless of the manufacture date. Transformer T-C1 must be K-13 rated and must have additional overload capacity for the nonlinear electronic loads of the Communications Room 116; no additional overload capacity is required for the other transformers.
1.9.6 Panelboards and Surge Protection
Panelboards must have copper bus, door-in-door hinged trim and bolt-on breakers. Provide external surge protective devices adjacent to MSB and LC1 with a maximum lead length of 3 feet, a surge counter and Form C dry contacts.
1.9.9 Operation and Maintenance Data
Submit operation and maintenance data in accordance with Section 01 78 23 OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE DATA and Army facility data in accordance with Section 01 78 24.00 10 FACILITY DATA REQUIREMENTS.
1.9.10 Short-Circuit Current Ratings
Provide panelboards with the following minimum short-circuit current ratings from the short-circuit study basis SCB-01 and the current utility data UP-4410 Rev 2: 480 V panelboards HM1 and H2A 14 kA rms symmetrical at 480 V; 480 V panelboards H1A and HE1 18 kA rms symmetrical at 480 V; 208 V panelboards LP1A, LP2A, LC1 and LE1 10 kA rms symmetrical at 208 V. Cordell Lighting Group - photometric file set for Building 4410
Issued 2026-04-17 by Vantia Photometric Laboratory.

Format
  Every file in this folder is an ANSI/IESNA LM-63-2002 photometric data file: plain ASCII, CRLF
  line endings, the identifier line IESNA:LM-63-2002, the required keyword block, and TILT=NONE.
  Photometric type 1 (Type C) with luminous opening dimensions in metres (units type 2). Vertical
  angles run 0 to 90 degrees in 5 degree steps; the candela rows are written one row per horizontal
  angle, each row holding one value for every vertical angle.

Basis of the numbers
  These are relative photometry files. The lumens-per-lamp field of the first data line is the RATED
  lamp lumens of the light engine, taken from the lamp data, not the measured output of the
  luminaire. The candela values are reported per those rated lamp lumens and already carry the
  luminaire efficiency, so the candela table integrates to less than the rated lamp lumens. The
  candela multiplier and the ballast factor are both 1.000 and have been applied to the tabulated
  values; no further multiplier is needed. Total luminaire lumens are not a field of the format -
  obtain them by integrating the candela table over solid angle (zonal lumen summation).
  Input watts on the second data line is the measured luminaire input power and is not adjusted by
  the ballast factor.

Provide and install each engine-generator set complete and totally functional, with all necessary ancillary equipment to include: air filtration; starting system; generator controls, protection, and isolation; instrumentation; lubrication; fuel system; cooling system; and engine exhaust system. Each engine-generator set must satisfy the requirements specified in the Engine-Generator Parameter Schedule. Submit certification that the engine-generator set and cooling system function properly in the ambient temperatures specified.
303:Maximum Speed. The maximum allowable speed for emergency standby applications is 1800 RPM. If there is not specific requirement or user requirement for slower speed machines, select 1800 RPM. Selection of the maximum 1800 RPM does not preclude provision of slower speed machines, for example, in the larger sizes (above 2000 kW), where 1800 RPM machines may not be available. However, for prime power or continuous duty plant applications, the lowest total cost of ownership would result by specifying a much lower speed, as recommended in UFC 3-540-04N, Section 5.1, Table 7. Lower speed engines require fewer overhauls, fewer oil changes, have a higher availability factor, and can be more fuel efficient. Even though prime duty power plants are the minority case, improper specification can result in very large increase in cost over the life of the installation. Frequently these plants are installed forward in contingency environments at FOBs or base camps which by nature demand reliable power at the lowest total cost. Furthermore, as prime sources of power these plants are relied upon as "the grid" and must perform as such for reliable power. Additionally, several manufacturers' medium speed (600-1200 RPM) engines will tolerate the varieties of fuel found in CONUS and OCONUS with minimal or no power or durability degradation.
308:Frequency Bandwidth. Governor frequency bandwidth defines the allowable steady state variation in frequency and is typically quite small for commercially available governors (typically less than plus or minus 0.4 percent with plus or minus 0.25 percent readily available). The predominant type of device loads which are susceptible to steady state frequency deviations less than plus or minus 0.4 percent are those which employ switching power supplies (computers and variable frequency drives).
309:Voltage Regulators. Solid state regulators are readily available which maintain the voltage level (regulation or voltage droop) to plus or minus 0.5 percent. Voltage regulator bandwidth is important relative primarily to transient response. EGSA Standard 100R-1992 defines three performance classes for voltage regulators: standard (2 percent bandwidth); high (1 percent bandwidth); and precision (0.5 percent bandwidth). Select the least restrictive bandwidth necessary to satisfy the application requirement.
312:Non-linear Loads: Non-linear loads are addressed in IEEE 519. They are loads that draw a non-sinusoidal current waveform when supplied by a sinusoidal voltage source. Typical non-linear loads include solid state switching power supplies, computer power supplies (including those found in desktop PC's, uninterruptible power supplies, variable frequency drives, radar power supplies, and solid state ballasts in fluorescent light fixtures. They cause distortion of the source voltage and current waveforms that can have harmful effects on many types of electrical equipment and electronics, including generators. Non-linear loads are similar to short circuits in that they provide momentary, sub-cycle-duration, short-circuiting of two phases. Switching power supplies consist of SCR/thyristor-controlled rectifier bridges which act as three single-phase loads, each connected across two phases of the power system. When the SCR/thyristors are switched on and off a notch in the voltage waveform will occur as a result of an instantaneous phase-phase short-circuit during the commutation of current. A low generator sub-transient reactance minimizes the voltage waveform distortion in the presence of such loads. For this reason when the non-linear loads comprise 25 percent or more of the loads served, the generator sub-transient reactance should be limited to no more than 0.12.

317:Maximum Step Load Increase. Maximum step load increase is used to account for the addition of block loads. These affect engine-generator set frequency and voltage output and usually initiate governor and regulator response. The change in engine-generator set output and the response of the governor and regulator defines the transient loading response. In the size range covered by this specification (and for standby applications) acquisition of full load in one step is typical for major engine-generator manufacturers (voltage deviation of 30 percent or less, frequency deviation of plus 5 percent, recovery time 3 to 5 seconds, typical). If the application requires a more stringent response, specify the actual maximum step load and add the allowable deviations and recovery times to the Engine Generator Set Parameter Schedule. If it is critical enough to add these requirements, also add the Transient Response Test to verify the results in the field. It should be noted that this adds significant cost to the cost of an engine-generator. Additionally, oversizing of engines causes maintenance problems and increases operating costs. The following percentages may be used when the actual load acquisition rate cannot be determined. Fluorescent lights can tolerate a maximum of 10 percent voltage variation. NEMA induction motors and control relays can tolerate a maximum of 10 percent variation, for 30 cycles and one cycle respectively. Solenoids (brakes, valves, clutches) and ac and dc starter coils can tolerate a maximum of minus 30 percent variation, for 1/2 cycle, 2 cycles (dropout), and 5 - 10 cycles (dropout) respectively.
323:Maximum Frequency Deviation. Computers can usually tolerate only plus or minus 0.5 Hz variation, so an UPS is normally required where computer services should not be interrupted, or where system recovery times are critical. Inverters can tolerate plus or minus 2 Hz variation. NEMA induction motors and control relays can tolerate a maximum of 5 percent frequency variation.

It must be understood that this definition uses the term "normal varying load condition factors". Most manufacturers use this terminology to indicate that their units typically are not rated for continuous operation at the nameplate rating, but rather that the units provided are rated for continuous operation at 70 to 80 percent of their nameplate rating, with periodic loading up to 100 percent of the nameplate rating for short (cyclical) periods during a power outage. def split_top_alts(s):
    """split s at top-level '][' boundaries -> list of alternative strings"""
    parts=[]; depth=0; cur=''
    i=0
    while i<len(s):
        if s[i]=='[': depth+=1; cur+='['
        elif s[i]==']':
            depth-=1; cur+=']'
        else:
            if depth==0 and s[i:i+2]=='][' :
                parts.append(cur); cur=''; i+=2; continue
            cur+=s[i]
        i+=1
    parts.append(cur)
    return [p for p in parts]

def strip_outer(a):
    a=a.strip()
    while a.startswith('[') and a.endswith(']') and matched(a):
        a=a[1:-1].strip()
    return a

def matched(a):
    d=0
    for i,ch in enumerate(a):
        if ch=='[': d+=1
        elif ch==']':
            d-=1
            if d==0 and i!=len(a)-1: return False
    return d==0

def parse_nodes(s):
    """return nested list: ('t',text) or ('c',[alt_nodes...])"""
    def parse_seq(i, stop):
        nodes=[]
        buf=''
        while i<len(s):
            ch=s[i]
            if ch=='[':
                if buf: nodes.append(('t',buf)); buf=''

                    elif c==']':

                        depth-=1; cur+=c; i+=1
                    elif depth==0 and s[i:i+2]=='][' :
                        alts.append(cur); cur=''; i+=2

def merge_adjacent(nodes):
    out=[]

Architect-Engineer Scope of Work — Electrical Design, Final (100 %) Submittal
Contract W912XX-27-C-0418 (PN 90417). Company Operations Facility (COF), Building 4410, Fort Calder, Georgia. U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Savannah District (fictional project).
1 GENERAL
1.1 Project. New two-story Company Operations Facility for an Army unit (Army project, new construction; no renovation). The facility is on an inland installation in Georgia; no state or local electrical amendments apply on the installation.
1.2 Delivery method. Design-bid-build. The A/E is the Designer of Record (DOR) and prepares the construction contract documents: drawings, specifications and the design analysis.
1.3 Scope of this task order. Prepare the Division 26 project specification sections listed in 3.9, and the electrical design basis workbook, for the final (100 %) submittal.
Table 1 — Electrical systems inventory (1.3). Present: main switchboard MSB; 480 V panelboards HM1, H1A, H2A, HE1; dry-type transformers T-1A, T-2A, T-C1, T-E1; 208 V panelboards LP1A, LP2A, LC1, LE1; engine-generator GEN-1; automatic transfer switches ATS-L (Article 700, bypass-isolation) and ATS-E (Article 702); advanced meter; SPDs at MSB and LC1; grounding electrode system with ground ring; lightning protection system; interior and exterior LED lighting; variable frequency drives on AHU-1 and AHU-2 (furnished under Division 23). Not in this project: busway; power cable tray; motor control centers; lighting control panelboards / relay panels; residential load centers; hazardous (classified) locations; 400 Hz systems; 270 V dc systems; medium-voltage work (utility furnishes primary); UPS (owner-furnished rack units only); photovoltaic system; paralleling switchgear; fire pump. Water service: HDPE (nonmetallic). Service entrance: underground, six 4 in PVC Schedule 40 ducts, concrete-encased, from the utility pad-mounted transformer to MSB; the secondary service conductors are sized by the Designer of Record in the design basis (3.4), and the conductors shown on E-601 Rev C are the 35 % submittal selection.
1.3.1 Government-furnished electrical coordination model. The Government furnishes, with the contract drawings, the electrical coordination model 50_bim/BLDG4410-E_RevC.ifc, an IFC4 (ISO 16739-1) model of the building authored in millimetres. The model is a contract document. It carries the building spaces and their dimensions, the electrical equipment locations, the interior luminaires of each space, and the routed feeder raceways, each raceway run identified by the feeder tag it carries. Dimensions, luminaire quantities and locations, routed feeder lengths and raceway trade sizes are taken from the model: they are not dimensioned or scheduled on the drawings. Also furnished are the LM-63 photometric files of the scheduled interior luminaire types, in 40_product_data/photometrics.
1.4 Schedule. Construction award April 2027; electrical equipment deliveries (switchboard, dry-type transformers, generator, transfer switch) June 2028; beneficial occupancy March 2029.
1.5 Order of precedence. Where requirements of the following documents differ, the order of precedence is: (1) this SOW; (2) Unified Facilities Criteria and federal regulations; (3) the installation standard IES-26; (4) the Owner's Project Requirements (current revision). A lower-precedence document may add or tighten a requirement; the more stringent requirement then governs unless the higher-precedence document prohibits it. Superseded revisions have no standing. Use only the current revisions listed in the transmittal log.
2 CRITERIA
2.1 Design to UFC 1-200-01, UFC 3-501-01, UFC 3-520-01 (current change), the federal regulations in the criteria folder, IES-26 and the OPR. NFPA 70 (edition adopted by UFC 1-200-01) applies but is not furnished. UFC 1-200-02 high performance and sustainable building requirements apply; no third-party certification is sought.
2.2 Use the Unified Facilities Guide Specifications (UFGS) Division 26 masters furnished in the guide specification library (August 2026 update). Other agencies' master specifications in the library are for reference only and must not be used as project specification text.
3 SPECIFICATION REQUIREMENTS
3.1 Tailoring. Tailor each UFGS for an Army design-bid-build project: keep only the Army tailoring options, resolve every bracketed choice and blank, delete notes to the specifier, and delete requirements for equipment and systems the project does not have.
3.2 Photometrics. The DOR provides the photometric calculations in the design analysis; the specifications must not require the Contractor to prepare photometric plans.
3.3 Format. UFS 1-300-02 is incorporated into this SOW and is binding for the project specifications regardless of its For-Information-Only status. English (inch-pound) units only. Deliver each section as a separate DOCX document (the Government converts them to Google Docs for review).
3.4 Ratings and delegated design. The panelboard and switchboard schedules on the drawings do not show short-circuit current ratings: state the minimum short-circuit current rating of the switchboard and of the 480 V and 208 V panelboards in the specifications, from the short-circuit study basis SCB-01 method and the current utility data. Seismic restraint of electrical equipment is a Contractor delegated design by a registered professional engineer; the DOR reviews it.
3.5 Power system studies. The Contractor performs the short-circuit, protective device coordination and arc flash studies on as-built data in accordance with Section 26 05 73 and provides device settings; the DOR reviews them. IES-26 Fort Calder Installation Electrical Design Standard — Revision 4
(February 2026)
Directorate of Public Works, Engineering Division. Applies to all new construction on Fort Calder. Where this standard
is more stringent than the Unified Facilities Criteria it governs; it never relaxes them.
1 General
1.3 No state or local electrical code amendments apply on the installation.
1.4 Site conditions: inland; no salt-spray or corrosive areas. Cooling design dry bulb (0.4 %) 97 F (36 C); maximum
recorded ambient 38 C; heating design dry bulb (99.6 %) 18 F (-8 C).
1.5 The electrical coordination model issued with the contract drawings (50_bim/BLDG4410-E_RevC.ifc) is a contract
document of equal standing with the drawings. Dimensions, equipment and luminaire locations, luminaire quantities
and routed raceway lengths are taken from that model; they are not dimensioned or scheduled on the drawings.
Where the model and a drawing disagree, report the discrepancy to the Contracting Officer before proceeding.
4 Wiring
4.1 Copper conductors only. 4.2 Insulation: feeders XHHW-2; branch circuits THHN/THWN-2.
4.3 Phase identification: 480Y/277 V brown, orange, yellow, neutral gray; 208Y/120 V black, red, blue, neutral white.
4.4 Metal-clad (MC) and armored (AC) cable are not permitted in new buildings.
4.5 Raceways: EMT concealed and above ceilings; RMC exposed below 8 ft in mechanical and electrical rooms and
exposed on building exteriors; PVC Schedule 40 underground and in slabs, with RMC or PVC-coated RMC elbows
and risers; liquidtight flexible metal conduit for final connections to vibrating equipment, 6 ft maximum. ENT, LFNC
and surface nonmetallic raceway are not permitted.
4.6 Raceway fill. Where more than two conductors are installed in one raceway, the sum of the overall cross-sectional
areas of the conductors must not exceed 40 percent of the interior cross-sectional area of the raceway. Take the
conductor overall areas from the project conductor data sheet CDS-7 and the raceway interior areas from the project
raceway data sheet RDS-1; the corresponding tables of NFPA 70 Chapter 9 are not reproduced in this standard and
are cited by designation only. Install each parallel conductor set of a feeder in its own raceway; a feeder run must not
carry more parallel sets than it has raceways. Count, in each raceway, three phase conductors, one neutral of the
same size as the phase conductors, and one equipment grounding conductor. Size the equipment grounding
conductor of a feeder the same size as the phase conductor where the phase conductor is smaller than 250 kcmil,
and one size smaller than the phase conductor in the CDS-7 size list where the phase conductor is 250 kcmil or
larger. Where a phase conductor is increased in size for voltage drop, increase the equipment grounding conductor
by the same rule.
4.7 Voltage drop. UFC 3-501-01 paragraph 3-2.7.1 governs and is adopted without change: 3 percent maximum for
feeders and service conductors, 3 percent maximum for branch circuits, and 5 percent maximum total from the point
of Government ownership to the furthest outlet. In addition, and more stringently, limit the voltage drop of any feeder
of the emergency system to 2 percent of nominal voltage. A feeder is a feeder of the emergency system when it
carries emergency system load, that is: the feeder from the normal source to the emergency system transfer switch;
the feeder from the alternate (engine-generator) source to that same transfer switch; and every feeder on the load
side of that transfer switch, including the primary and secondary feeders of any transformer serving emergency
system load. The emergency system transfer switch is the transfer switch shown on the one-line diagram as serving
NFPA 70 Article 700 loads. Feeders serving only optional standby (NFPA 70 Article 702) load are not feeders of the
emergency system and keep the UFC allowance, as do the service conductors, which are not feeders. Calculate

Fort Calder DPW   Page 2
feeder voltage drop over the one-way routed length of the feeder.
5 Distribution equipment
5.1 Panelboards: copper bus, door-in-door hinged trim, bolt-on breakers.
5.2 Surge protective devices: external units mounted adjacent to the protected equipment, 3 ft maximum lead length,
with surge counter and Form C dry contacts.
5.4 Nameplates: normal power black letters on white; emergency and standby power white letters on red.
6 Grounding
6.1 Building grounding electrode system resistance: 10 ohms maximum, measured by the fall-of-potential method.
7 Seismic
7.2 Designated seismic systems: the engine-generator set, the emergency (life-safety) transfer switch and distribution
(ATS-L, T-E1, LE1) and emergency system raceways. Component importance factor Ip = 1.5 for designated seismic
systems and 1.0 for other electrical components.
8 Metering
8.1 Advanced electric meter at the building main switchboard, Modbus TCP to the installation meter data
management system (MDMS), 15-minute interval data. No other remote communication from the switchboard. Meter:
three-phase 4-wire transformer-rated socket meter, Form 9S, ANSI C12.20 accuracy class 0.2, with test switch.
Detailed ASHRAE 90.1 energy monitoring is not authorized.
9 Testing
9.1 Acceptance testing to NETA ATS by an independent NETA-accredited company with a NETA Level III lead
technician. Scope: switchboard MSB; 480 V panelboards; dry-type transformers; feeders 100 A and larger (insulation
resistance); grounding electrode system (fall-of-potential); SPDs; ground-fault protection on the main; generator and
transfer switch (26 32 15 / 26 36 23 field tests witnessed).
9.2 Power system studies are modelled in SKM PowerTools; deliver the native model files.
10 Engine-generators and transfer switches
10.1 Fuel: ultra-low-sulfur No. 2 diesel; biodiesel blends are not permitted. NFPA 110 designation: Class equal to the
required on-site runtime in hours, Type 10, Level 1 for systems supplying NFPA 70 Article 700 loads.
10.2 On-site fuel: 72 hours at full load minimum in a UL 142 double-wall sub-base tank with leak detection; the
installation fuel delivery contract provides the remainder of seven days.
10.3 Sound: 72 dBA maximum at 23 ft from the enclosure.
10.4 Emissions: EPA-certified emergency stationary engine (40 CFR 60 Subpart IIII); covered by the installation air
permit - no project air permit; the Contractor submits the EPA engine certificate to the installation environmental
office.
10.5 Field test: 4-hour resistive load bank test at 100 % of the nameplate kW rating.
10.6 Transfer switches: 4-pole, open transition with in-phase monitor. Separate transfer switches for the emergency
system (NFPA 70 Article 700) and for optional standby loads; the optional standby switch transfers 30 seconds after


--- page 3 ---
IES-26 Rev 4
Fort Calder DPW   Page 3
the emergency switch.
10.7 Generator performance class: ISO 8528 class G2. Engine-generator transient performance is further limited for
this installation as follows, and these limits are the project's requirement wherever the guide specification asks the
designer to insert a value. On any load step of the step-load sequence, whether that step is the application or the
rejection of load: the transient voltage dip must not exceed 15 percent of rated voltage; the set must recover to within
2 percent of rated voltage within 3 seconds of the step; and the transient frequency deviation must not exceed 5
percent of rated frequency. These limits are more stringent than the envelope quoted in the guide specification for
engine-generator sets (which contemplates up to 30 percent voltage deviation and a recovery time of 3 to 5 seconds
for a set taking full load in one step); the more stringent installation requirement governs. Demonstrate compliance by
the step-load sequence prepared under the project's generator step-load basis, and verify it at the field test.

connection to the utility monitoring and control system.
11.4 Exterior lighting: 3000 K maximum; CRI 70 minimum; parking-lot luminaires B2-U0-G2 maximum, wall packs
B1-U0-G1; optical compartment IP66; driver surge protection 10 kV/10 kA; ANSI C136.41 7-pin receptacle on
pole-mounted luminaires; aluminum anchor-base poles on concrete foundations; controls: astronomic time clock with
photosensor, curfew dimming to 30 % from 23:00 to 05:00.

--- page 1 ---
GSB-01 Rev 1
Harlan Sato Engineers LLC (A/E, Designer of Record)   Page 1
GSB-01 Generator Step-Load Basis — Building 4410 (Rev 1)
Harlan Sato Engineers LLC (A/E, Designer of Record). Establishes the method by which the sequence in which load
is placed on the standby engine-generator GEN-1 is developed and verified. This memorandum states the method
and the input data only; it states no transient voltage dip, no recovery time and no step sequence.
1. Scope
On loss of the normal source the engine-generator starts and the transfer switches transfer their loads to it. The load
is not placed on the set all at once: it is placed in steps. The step-load sequence is a design deliverable. Each step is
a group of load tags placed on the set at the same instant; the steps are taken in order, the set recovering to steady
state between steps.
2. Load data
The loads that transfer to the engine-generator, the running kVA and the starting (locked-rotor) kVA of each, and the
transfer switch that serves each, are scheduled on the mechanical equipment schedule M-601 (sheet 'Generator
transfer loads') and, for the motor-driven equipment, in the nameplate data of sheet 'M-601'. Machine data for the set
are on the manufacturer's data sheet GEN-1. Acceptance limits are in the installation electrical design standard
IES-26 paragraph 10.7.
3. Transient voltage dip of a step
Calculate the transient voltage dip caused by one step as
    dip (per cent) = 100 x Xd2 x kVA(step) / ( kVA(alternator) + Xd2 x ( kVA(step) + kVA(running) ) )
in which Xd2 is the saturated direct-axis subtransient reactance of the alternator in per unit on its own kVA base, from
data sheet GEN-1 (0.12 per unit); kVA(alternator) is the standby kVA rating of the set from data sheet GEN-1 (187.5
kVA); kVA(step) is the sum of the starting (locked-rotor) kVA of every load tag added at that step; and kVA(running) is
the sum of the running kVA of every load tag already carried by the set immediately before that step. For the first step
kVA(running) is zero.
A load that is not motor-driven has a starting kVA equal to its running kVA, as scheduled. Use the scheduled
locked-rotor kVA as it is; do not apply a starting-current multiplier of your own and do not apply a reduced-voltage
starting credit, since no unit is scheduled with a reduced-voltage starter.
4. Recovery time of a step
Take the time for the set to recover from a step as
    t(recovery, seconds) = 0.6 + 0.08 x dip (per cent)
using the dip of paragraph 3 for that step, expressed in per cent. The recovery time of every step must satisfy the limit
of IES-26 paragraph 10.7.
5. Rules the sequence must satisfy
a. Every load that transfers to the engine-generator must appear in the sequence exactly once. A load may not be
started twice and no load may be omitted.
b. Every load of the emergency system, that is every load served by the emergency (life safety) transfer switch, which
is the transfer switch identified on E-601 as serving NFPA 70 Article 700 loads, must be carried by the first step. The
emergency transfer switch restores its loads within 10 seconds of loss of the normal source (IES-26 paragraph 10.6),


--- page 2 ---
GSB-01 Rev 1
Harlan Sato Engineers LLC (A/E, Designer of Record)   Page 2
so its loads cannot wait for a later step. Optional standby loads may be placed on any step.
c. The transient voltage dip of every step must not exceed the limit of IES-26 paragraph 10.7.
d. The total running load carried by the set when every load has transferred, taken as the sum of the running kVA of
all transferred loads multiplied by the rated power factor of the set from data sheet GEN-1 (0.8), must not exceed the
standby kilowatt rating of the set (150 kW).
e. A step may not be empty.
6. Deliverable
State the sequence as an ordered list of steps, each step being the list of load tags of M-601 placed on the set at that
step. Report, for each step, the summed starting kVA, the running kVA carried before the step, the transient voltage
dip and the recovery time. Any sequence that satisfies paragraph 5 is acceptable; where the number of steps is an
objective, the fewest steps that satisfy paragraph 5 is the target.
====

import re, json, sys, os
BASE='/tmp/ahpele/corpus/final_batch4__electrical_task8_electrical_specs__blind/20_guide_specifications/UFGS_Division_26_PDF/'
FOOT=re.compile(r'^SECTION \d\d \d\d \d\d\s+Page \d+$')
AST=re.compile(r'^\*{10,}\s*$')
def parse(num):
    raw=open(BASE+'UFGS %s.pdf.txt'%num).read().split('\n')
    # drop through end of TOC
    start=0
    for i,l in enumerate(raw):
        if 'End of Section Table of Contents' in l:
            start=i+1; break
    lines=raw[start:]
    paras=[]; buf=''; in_note=False
    for l in lines:
        s=l.rstrip('\n')
        if s.startswith('--- page '): continue
        if AST.match(s.strip()):
            in_note=not in_note; continue
        if in_note: continue
        if not s.strip(): continue
        if FOOT.match(s.strip()): continue
        if re.match(r'^(USACE / NAVFAC / AFCEC|UFGS-\d\d \d\d \d\d|Change \d+ - \d\d/\d\d|Preparing Activity:|Superseding|UNIFIED FACILITIES GUIDE SPECIFICATIONS|References are in agreement|DIVISION 26 - ELECTRICAL)',s.strip()):
            continue
        wrapped = s.endswith(' ') or s.endswith('\t')
        t=s.strip()
        if buf:
            buf=buf+' '+t
        else:
            buf=t
        if not wrapped:
            paras.append(re.sub(r'\s+',' ',buf).strip()); buf=''
    if buf: paras.append(re.sub(r'\s+',' ',buf).strip())
    return [p for p in paras if p]
if __name__=='__main__':
    for num in sys.argv[1:]:
        ps=parse(num)
        json.dump(ps,open('/tmp/ahpele/work/spec2/%s.paras.json'%num,'w'),indent=0)
        print(num,len(ps))
EOF

The System Verifier may inspect and record settings, markings, and otherwise document the existing equipment. The System Verifier may also place appropriate hazard labels on equipment. When working with energized equipment, the system verifier must be a Qualified Person per NFPA 70E or working under the direct supervision of a Qualified Person. The System Verifier may communicate with the system owner to determine if the equipment within the studied system has received maintenance and testing in accordance with NETA MTS or NFPA 70B.
1.5 PROJECT REQUIREMENTS
1.5.1 Scope of the Studies
The power system covered by this specification is the Building 4410 electrical distribution system, from the 1000 kVA, 12.47 kV - 480Y/277 V utility service transformer secondary through every 480 V and 208 V bus: MSB, HM1, H1A, H2A, ATS-E, HE1, ATS-L, LP1A, LP2A, LC1 and LE1.

Model the studies in SKM PowerTools and deliver the native model files. Coordinate the protective devices to achieve selective coordination; electronic trip breakers are used for that purpose.
1.5.2 System Analyzer Qualifications
The System Analyzer must be a registered professional engineer with not less than 5 years of power system study experience, and must seal the study reports.
1.5.3 Study Outputs

Use the results of the load flow study to perform the fault current study in accordance with IEEE 3002.3. Provide balanced three-phase fault, bolted line-to-line fault, and single line-to-ground fault current values at each voltage transformation point and at each power distribution bus. For each location, show in tabular form on the diagram or in the report the maximum and minimum available fault currents of all modes of operation for that location.
Where the available fault current at the source bus is not available, describe how the fault contribution from the source bus was determined and why this method is reasonable for the study.
3.2.6 System Coordination Study
Use the results of the load flow study and fault current study. For normal modes of operation, demonstrate that selectivity has been obtained between the devices within the scope of the project. Demonstrate the equipment, machines, and conductors are protected from damage from overloads and fault conditions. Include a description of the coordination of the protective devices in this project. Provide a written narrative describing which devices may operate in the event of a fault at each bus; the logic used to arrive at device ratings and settings; situations where system coordination is not achievable due to device limitations; coordination between upstream and downstream devices; and relay settings. Provide recommendations to improve or enhance system reliability, and detail where such changes would involve additions or modifications to the contract and cost damages (addition or reduction). Provide composite coordination plots on a log-log scale. Where recommendations are provided to improve or enhance system reliability, provide separate coordination plots on log-log scale showing the system coordination before and after the implementation of the recommendations. Where coordination has been adjusted to lower arc flash values, include a discussion of the change and the impact on the system within the report.
3.2.7 Arc Flash Hazard Study
Perform the arc flash hazard study in accordance with IEEE 1584.1. Utilize the data from the fault current study to determine the worst case incident energy per IEEE 1584, IEEE C2, and OSHA 29 CFR 1910.269 Appendix E. Use identified modes of operation to determine the worst case arc flash energy. If not included in another study, include a description of the devices and device settings for the operating modes that provided the highest arc flash energy. The use of a "maintenance switch" to temporarily reduce the Arc Flash incident energy for maintenance work is acceptable. Where the arc flash energies exceed 1.2 cal/cm2 provide recommendations to reduce the arc flash energy to 1.2 cal/cm2.
Where the AC system voltage is 208 volts or less with an available short-circuit current less than 2000 A, an arc flash hazard study is not required.
3.2.8 Study report(s)
a. Include a narrative describing the studies performed; the bases and methods used; and the desired method of coordinated protection of the power system.
b. Include descriptive and technical data for existing devices and new protective devices proposed. Include manufacturers published data, nameplate data, and definition of the fixed or adjustable features of the existing or new protective devices. For existing devices, included statements on the condition of the equipment based upon field inspections and owner's statements and reports.
c. Document utility company data including system voltages, fault MVA, system X/R ratio, time-current characteristic curves, current transformer ratios, and relay device numbers and settings; and existing power system data including time-current characteristic curves and protective device ratings and settings. Identify all assumptions about the protection devices, equipment, and system where data was not available.
d. For each bus in the system, provide fully coordinated composite time-current characteristics (TCC) curves as required to ensure coordinated power system protection between protective devices and equipment. In a tabular format, provide existing and recommended ratings and settings of all protective devices.
e. Provide an arc flash study report in accordance with IEEE 1584.1.
f. Provide the calculations performed for the studies, including computer programs utilized. Provide the name of the software package, developer, and version number.
g. The System Analyzer must stamp the study reports.
3.2.9 Arc Flash Labels
Provide arc flash warning labels on electrical equipment likely to require examination, servicing, or maintenance while energized. Typical types of equipment include pad-mounted transformers, switchgear, switchboards, panelboards, disconnect switches, industrial control panels, meter socket enclosures, and motor control centers that are in other than dwelling occupancies. The arc flash label naming must match the naming used in the system modeling and the single line diagram.
Comply with the label requirements specified in NFPA 70E. Obtain approval of arc flash label formats before printing.
a. Provide a 3.5 inch x 5 inch to 4 inch x 6 inch thermal transfer type label of high adhesion polyester for each location device analyzed. The label must remain in place and be legible for at least 5 years in the installed environment.
b. Labels must be machine printed with no field markings. Provide arc flash labels in the following manner. All labels must be based on implemented overcurrent devices and settings.
1. Provide at least one arc flash label for each 480 volt and 208 volt panelboards.
2. Provide at least one arc flash label for each low voltage (less than 1000 V) switchboard.
3. Where the equipment construction has different hazards levels in different areas, provide a label for each compartment, cubicle, or section separated by barriers
c. Use the worst case hazard of all operating scenarios unless mitigation procedures are used. If mitigation procedures are used, explain the procedures on the label.
3.3 MODELING
Develop a software model of the electrical system identified in the scope of the studies. Use the latest version of SKM PowerTools(TM). Develop the model with accurate, verified information. Model existing electrical equipment, machines, devices, and conductors directly connected to, altered by, or otherwise affected by the work. This includes, but is not limited to generators, transformers, switchgear, switchboards, panelboards, motor control centers, motors, voltage regulators, tap changers, protective relays, circuit breakers, switches, fuses, conductors, capacitors, reactors, grounding system, and control equipment.
Provide the final model files in their native editable formats for future use by the Government. Include device information for devices not in the software vendor's standard distribution.

(10) Confirm correct application of manufacturer's recommended lubricants.
(11) Inspect insulators for evidence of physical damage or contaminated surfaces.
(12) Verify correct barrier installation and operation.
(13) Exercise all active components.
(14) Inspect all mechanical indicating devices for correct operation.

--- page 1 ---
PCB-01 Rev 1
Harlan Sato Engineers LLC (A/E, Designer of Record)   Page 1
PCB-01 Photometric Calculation Basis — Building 4410 (Rev 1)
Harlan Sato Engineers LLC (A/E, Designer of Record). Establishes the method by which the interior illuminance of
every space of Building 4410 is calculated and by which a luminaire quantity is verified. This memorandum states the
method and the input data only; it states no calculated illuminance, uniformity, lighting power density or luminaire
quantity.
1. Governing criteria
Section 26 51 00 requires computer-generated photometric plans for each space, using the applicable light loss
factor, to verify that the proposed luminaires and locations meet the required performance criteria. That section
establishes, for the calculation: horizontal illuminance taken at a maximum of every one foot (305 mm) across the
task area; a recommended light loss factor of 0.81 for LED luminaires; uniformity calculated as the ratio of the
average calculated illuminance over the minimum calculated illuminance of the calculation grid; and a 10 percent
margin of error on each target, a 'Minimum Average' being an average taken over the entire task area that may not be
less than the stated value within that margin.
The target illumination levels for each interior application, in the 'Minimum Average' and 'Uniformity' vocabulary of that
section, are given in the installation electrical design standard IES-26 paragraph 11.6. The whole-building interior
lighting power density limit is IES-26 paragraph 11.7. Surface reflectances are scheduled on A-601. Room
dimensions, ceiling heights, luminaire positions and luminaire quantities are taken from the electrical coordination
model 50_bim/BLDG4410-E_RevC.ifc.
The light loss factor used for every LED luminaire in this project is 0.81. The margin of error applied to each target is
10 percent: a calculated average maintained illuminance is acceptable when it is not less than 0.9 times the Minimum
Average of IES-26 paragraph 11.6, and a calculated uniformity is acceptable when it is not more than 1.1 times the
Uniformity limit of that paragraph.
2. Luminous flux of a luminaire: zonal integration of the candela table
Each interior luminaire type is described by an LM-63 photometric file named in the luminaire schedule E-501 and
issued in 40_product_data/photometrics/. The candela table of that file gives, for each horizontal angle present in the
file, the luminous intensity in candelas at the vertical angles 0 to 90 degrees from nadir in 5 degree steps.
The luminous flux of the luminaire to be used in this calculation is the flux obtained by integrating that candela table. It
is NOT the rated lamp lumens written in the file header and it is NOT the rated lamp lumens scheduled on E-501;
those are lamp values and are larger than the flux the luminaire emits. Obtain the flux as follows.
a. For each vertical angle in the table, form the mean intensity over the horizontal angles. Where the file contains a
single horizontal plane, the mean is that plane's value at that vertical angle. Where the file contains more than one
horizontal plane, take the trapezoidal average over the horizontal angles present: sum, over each adjacent pair of
horizontal angles a and b, the quantity (I(a) + I(b)) / 2 multiplied by (b - a); then divide that sum by (the last horizontal
angle minus the first horizontal angle). The files are quadrant symmetric and carry horizontal angles from 0 to 90
degrees.
b. Sum the zonal contributions over the vertical angles. For each adjacent pair of vertical angles t1 and t2, add
    2 x pi x (cos t1 - cos t2) x (Ibar(t1) + Ibar(t2)) / 2
in which Ibar is the mean intensity of step (a) at that vertical angle and the angles are in radians. The sum over all
adjacent pairs is the luminous flux of one luminaire, in lumens.
3. Intensity at an arbitrary direction: bilinear interpolation


--- page 2 ---
PCB-01 Rev 1
Harlan Sato Engineers LLC (A/E, Designer of Record)   Page 2
The intensity at a vertical angle theta from nadir and a horizontal angle phi is interpolated bilinearly from the candela
table. Fold the horizontal angle into the range 0 to 90 degrees by quadrant symmetry: take the absolute value, reduce
modulo 180 degrees and, if the result exceeds 90 degrees, replace it by 180 degrees minus the result. Interpolate
linearly between the two bounding horizontal planes of the file, and linearly between the two bounding vertical angles
of the table (the vertical angles are evenly spaced, so the fraction is the remainder of theta divided by the step,
divided by the step). Where the file contains a single horizontal plane, no horizontal interpolation is made. The
intensity is zero at and above 90 degrees from nadir.
4. Calculation grid and work plane
The work plane is a horizontal plane 2.5 feet above the finished floor of the space. The calculation grid covers the
whole floor area of the space, which is the task area for these targets.
Grid points are spaced 1 foot apart on each horizontal axis, and the first point on each axis is 0.5 foot from the wall.
On an axis of extent E feet the number of points is therefore floor((E - 2 x 0.5) / 1) + 1, not less than one, and the
points lie at the room origin on that axis plus 0.5 plus 1 times 0, 1, 2 and so on. The grid is the full cross product of the
points of the two axes. Take the room extents and the room origin from the coordination model.
5. Direct component
Let h be the mounting height of the luminaires above the work plane: the height of the luminaire above the finished
floor of its storey, taken directly from the placement of the luminaire in the coordination model, less the work plane
height of paragraph 4. All luminaires of one space are at the same height. Where h is not positive the space cannot
be calculated by this method.
For each grid point, sum over every luminaire in the space the quantity
    I(theta, phi) x (h / d) / (d x d)
in which, writing dx and dy for the horizontal offsets from the luminaire to the grid point: d = sqrt(dx x dx + dy x dy + h
x h) is the slant distance; theta = atan(sqrt(dx x dx + dy x dy) / h) is the vertical angle from nadir; and phi = atan(|dy| /
|dx|) is the horizontal angle, measured from the long axis of the luminaire, which is the +X axis of the coordination
model for every modelled interior luminaire. Where the grid point is directly under the luminaire take phi as zero;
where dx is zero and dy is not, take phi as 90 degrees. The factor (h / d) is the cosine of the angle of incidence, so the
expression is the inverse-square-cosine illuminance in footcandles when I is in candelas and the distances are in feet.
Multiply the sum at each grid point by the light loss factor 0.81 to obtain the direct component of the maintained
illuminance at that point. The average direct component is the arithmetic mean of the direct component over all grid
points.
6. Interreflected component
The interreflected component is uniform over the space and is obtained from the flux that does not reach the work
plane directly, redistributed by the average reflectance of the room surfaces:
    E(indirect) = rho / (1 - rho) x (PHI x LLF - E(direct, average) x A(work plane)) / A(room)
in which PHI is the luminous flux of one luminaire from paragraph 2 multiplied by the number of luminaires in the
space; LLF is 0.81; E(direct, average) is the average direct component of paragraph 5; A(work plane) is the floor area
of the space; and A(room) is the total area of the room surfaces, taken as
    A(room) = 2 x A(floor) + 2 x H x (W + D)
with W and D the room extents and H the finished ceiling height, all from the coordination model. The term in brackets
is taken as zero if it would be negative.


--- page 3 ---
PCB-01 Rev 1
Harlan Sato Engineers LLC (A/E, Designer of Record)   Page 3
rho is the area-weighted average reflectance of the room surfaces,
    rho = (rho(ceiling) x A(floor) + rho(floor) x A(floor) + rho(wall) x 2 x H x (W + D)) / A(room)
using the ceiling, wall and floor reflectances scheduled for that room on A-601.
7. Reported quantities
The average maintained illuminance of the space is the average direct component plus the interreflected component.
The minimum maintained illuminance is the smallest direct component over the grid plus the interreflected
component. The uniformity is the average maintained illuminance divided by the minimum maintained illuminance.
The lighting power density of the space is the number of luminaires multiplied by the scheduled input watts of the
type, divided by the floor area of the space. The whole-building interior lighting power density is the total input watts of
all interior luminaires of the building divided by the total interior floor area of all spaces, and is compared with the limit
of IES-26 paragraph 11.7.
8. Re-layout where a quantity is revised
Where the calculation confirms the luminaire quantity shown in the coordination model, the luminaire positions of the
model govern and are used as they are.
Where a different quantity n is evaluated for a space, do not attempt to preserve the modelled positions: lay the n
luminaires out again on a uniform grid over the whole space, by the following rule. Take the number of columns
(along the X axis of the space) as the nearest whole number to sqrt(n x W / D), not less than one and not more than
n, in which W and D are the room extents along X and Y. Take the number of rows as n divided by the number of
columns, rounded up to a whole number. Place the luminaires at the centres of the cells of that row-by-column grid:
the luminaire in row r and column c, counting r and c from zero, is at
    x = X(origin) + W x (c + 0.5) / columns,  y = Y(origin) + D x (r + 0.5) / rows
filling row by row, and keep the first n positions so generated. The mounting height is unchanged. This rule is used for
every space and every quantity so that two engineers evaluating the same quantity obtain the same layout.
9. Data sources
Candela tables: the LM-63 file named for each type on E-501. Input watts, type marks and descriptions: E-501.
Surface reflectances: A-601. Room extents, ceiling heights, luminaire quantities, luminaire positions and luminaire
mounting heights: the coordination model 50_bim/BLDG4410-E_RevC.ifc. Illuminance targets and uniformity limits:
IES-26 paragraph 11.6. Lighting power density limit: IES-26 paragraph 11.7. Light loss factor, grid spacing, uniformity
definition and margin of error: Section 26 51 00 and this memorandum.

import json, math, re, numpy as np
from collections import defaultdict
D=json.load(open('ifc_extract.json'))
spaces={s['id']:s for s in D['spaces']}
lums=defaultdict(list)
for l in D['lums']: lums[l['room']].append(l)

def readies(path):
    lines=open(path,errors='ignore').read().replace('\r','').split('\n')
    i=[k for k,l in enumerate(lines) if l.strip().startswith('TILT=')][0]
    a=lines[i+1].split()
    nl=float(a[0]); lum=float(a[1]); mult=float(a[2]); nv=int(a[3]); nh=int(a[4])
    bf=float(lines[i+2].split()[0]); watts=float(lines[i+2].split()[2])
    va=[float(x) for x in ' '.join(lines[i+3:i+3+ (nv+9)//10]).split()][:nv]
    k=i+3+(nv+9)//10
    ha=[float(x) for x in ' '.join(lines[k:k+(nh+9)//10]).split()][:nh]
    k=k+(nh+9)//10
    vals=[]
    toks=[]
    for l in lines[k:]:
        toks+=l.split()
        if len(toks)>=nv*nh: break
    vals=np.array([float(x) for x in toks[:nv*nh]]).reshape(nh,nv)*mult*bf
    return dict(va=va,ha=ha,v=vals,flux=None,watts=watts)

def flux(ies):
    va=ies['va']; v=ies['v']; ha=ies['ha']
    # mean over horizontal angles
    if len(ha)==1:
        Ibar=v[0]
    else:
        s=np.zeros(len(va))
        for j in range(len(ha)-1):
            s+=(v[j]+v[j+1])/2*(ha[j+1]-ha[j])
        Ibar=s/(ha[-1]-ha[0])
    F=0
    for k in range(len(va)-1):
        t1=math.radians(va[k]); t2=math.radians(va[k+1])
        F+=2*math.pi*(math.cos(t1)-math.cos(t2))*(Ibar[k]+Ibar[k+1])/2
    return F

def I(ies,th,ph):
    va=ies['va']; ha=ies['ha']; v=ies['v']
    ph=abs(ph)%180
    if ph>90: ph=180-ph
    # horizontal
    if len(ha)==1:
        row=np.array([v[0][j] for j in range(len(va))],dtype=float)
    else:
        if ph<=ha[0]: j=0; fr=0
        elif ph>=ha[-1]: j=len(ha)-2; fr=1
        else:
            j=int(np.searchsorted(ha,ph)-1); fr=(ph-ha[j])/(ha[j+1]-ha[j])
        row=(1-fr)*v[j]+fr*v[j+1]
    if th<=va[0]: return float(row[0])
    if th>=va[-1]: return 0.0
    k=int(np.searchsorted(va,th)-1); fr=(th-va[k])/(va[k+1]-va[k])
    return float((1-fr)*row[k]+fr*row[k+1])

def layout(n,W,Dd,x0,y0):
    cols=max(1,min(n,round(math.sqrt(n*W/Dd))))
    rows=math.ceil(n/cols)
    pts=[]
    for r in range(rows):
        for c in range(cols):
            pts.append((x0+W*(c+0.5)/cols, y0+Dd*(r+0.5)/rows))
    return pts[:n]

def calc(room,n,typ,use_model):
    s=spaces[room]; W,Dd,H,x0,y0,z0=s['W'],s['D'],s['H'],s['x0'],s['y0'],s['z0']
    ml=lums[room]
    if use_model:
        pos=[(l['x'],l['y'],l['z']) for l in ml][:n]
    else:
        pts=layout(n,W,Dd,x0,y0)
        h0=ml[0]['z']
        pos=[(x,y,h0) for x,y in pts]
    h=pos[0][2]/1 - z0 - 2.5
    # grid
    nx=int(math.floor(W-1))+1; ny=int(math.floor(Dd-1))+1
    xs=[x0+0.5+i for i in range(nx)]; ys=[y0+0.5+j for j in range(ny)]
    E=np.zeros((ny,nx))
    for (lx,ly,lz) in pos:
        for j,y in enumerate(ys):
            for i,x in enumerate(xs):
                dx=x-lx; dy=y-ly
                r=math.hypot(dx,dy); d=math.hypot(r,h)
                th=math.degrees(math.atan2(r,h))
                if r==0: ph=0
                elif dx==0: ph=90
                else: ph=math.degrees(math.atan2(abs(dy),abs(dx)))
                E[j,i]+=I(ies[typ],th,ph)*(h/d)/(d*d)
    E*=0.81
    Ed=E.mean()
    gc,wc=A601[room]; fc=0.20
    A=W*Dd
    Ar=2*A+2*H*(W+Dd)
    rho=(gc*A+fc*A+wc*2*H*(W+Dd))/Ar
    term=ies[typ]['flux']*n*0.81-Ed*A
    term=max(term,0)
    Eind=rho/(1-rho)*term/Ar
    avg=Ed+Eind; mn=E.min()+Eind
    return avg,mn,avg/mn,n*ies[typ]['watts']/A

=== F02
   finding_id : F02
   document : BLDG4410-E_RevC.ifc coordination model, Rev C
   location : Luminaire quantities in all 36 interior spaces
   defect : The luminaire quantities carried in the model total 11,290 W over 38,400 sq ft, a whole-building interior lighting power density of 0.294 W/ft2, which exceeds the IES-26 11.7 limit of 0.285 W/ft2. Several spaces also miss the IES-26 11.6 illuminance targets (Open Office A 22.6 fc against 30 fc; Communications Room 21.1 fc against 30 fc).
   correction : Quantities re-established per PCB-01 paragraph 8 (uniform re-layout of each revised quantity) as the smallest quantity meeting each space Minimum Average and uniformity target of IES-26 11.6 outright. Revised design 10,905 W and 0.284 W/ft2, which meets IES-26 11.7 (0.285 W/ft2).
=== F03
   finding_id : F03
   document : E-601 Power One-Line Diagram, Rev C (5 August 2026)
   location : Feeder MSB note: (6) sets 4-#600 CU
   defect : The 35 percent submittal selection of six sets of 600 kcmil gives 2,520 A allowable ampacity for a 1,250 A design load (50 percent over) and reduces the service conductor impedance so that the calculated available fault current at MSB rises to 18.03 kA, which would force a 22 kA switchboard rating. E-601 general note 3 requires the selection to be verified against the routed length in the model.
   correction : Service conductors re-sized to six sets of 300 kcmil copper: 1,710 A allowable ampacity, which is not less than both the 1,250 A design load of FDB-01 Table 1 and the 1,600 A main device rating of the service entrance switchboard (so the service conductors are protected at their ampacity); 1.17 percent voltage drop and 17.6 percent fill. This gives 17.93 kA available at MSB and an 18 kA switchboard rating. Six sets of 250 kcmil (1,530 A) would meet the 1,250 A design load but would be smaller than the 1,600 A main device and are therefore not used.
=== F13
   finding_id : F13
   document : Unified Facilities Guide Specification 26 24 13 (August 2021) and 26 32 15 (February 2026)
   location : Articles 3.2 and 3.7 grounding electrode resistance
   defect : The guide texts state a grounding electrode resistance not exceeding 25 ohms (switchboard section) and 5 ohms (generator section), and 5 ohms was also the withdrawn value of OPR Rev A. IES-26 6.1 requires 10 ohms maximum and OPR Rev B paragraph 7 states that the 5 ohm value is withdrawn and that IES-26 governs.
   correction : Both guide values replaced by the 10 ohm maximum of IES-26 6.1 in Sections 26 24 13 and 26 32 15; the more stringent or otherwise applicable value is applied consistently across the Division 26 sections.
=== F12
   finding_id : F12
   document : E-601 Power One-Line Diagram, Rev C
   location : feeder H2A
   defect : The model run CND-H2A-1 has eight segments and a developed length of 91 ft against 12 to 26 ft for the other panel feeders; the length is used as modelled because the coordination model is a contract document.
   correction : Length of 91 ft used in the H2A voltage-drop calculation: 0.56 percent of 480 V, within the 3 percent allowance. No change.

1.3 SUBMITTALS
3.2.1 Scope of Studies
The scope of the studies begins at the source bus and extends down to the system buses where the available fault current is 10,000 amperes or less (symmetrical) and at most 600 volts for facility-level distribution buses. For this project the studies cover the 1000 kVA, 12.47 kV - 480Y/277 V utility
1. Normal operation, with the utility source supplying the building and the engine-generator disconnected from the bus.
2. Generator operation, with the engine-generator supplying the emergency system through ATS-L and the optional standby system through ATS-E, and the utility source disconnected.

Determine and document the time-current characteristics, features, ratings, ampacities, and nameplate data for each existing protective device, electrical equipment, and feeder cables. steps.message:
All deliverables are present, complete and validated. Final verification:

## Files at the required path
`/filesystem/final_batch4__electrical_task8_electrical_specs__blind/output/submission.zip` (171 KB) contains exactly:

| member | type | content |
|---|---|---|
| `specs/26 05 73.docx` | DOCX | POWER SYSTEM STUDIES (2,637 words) |
| `specs/26 20 00.docx` | DOCX | INTERIOR DISTRIBUTION SYSTEM (10,495 words) |
| `specs/26 24 13.docx` | DOCX | SWITCHBOARDS (4,561 words) |
| `specs/26 32 15.docx` | DOCX | ENGINE-GENERATOR SET, STATIONARY (STANDBY) (25,183 words) |
| `specs/26 36 23.docx` | DOCX | AUTOMATIC TRANSFER SWITCHES (4,777 words) |
| `specs/26 51 00.docx` | DOCX | INTERIOR LIGHTING (8,316 words) |
| `design_basis.xlsx` | XLSX | Sections (6), Feeders (17), ShortCircuit (11), Photometric (36), StepLoad (3), Register (83), Findings (17), Summary (13 rows) |

## Validation results
- `python3 /tmp/ahpele/bin/ahpele_check.py submission.zip` → **no problems found** (zip, six DOCX packages, XLSX).
- Workbook schema check → every required column of every required sheet present; **0 blank required cells**; one record per row.
- `ahpele_reqscan.py --check` → **803/803** strong candidates reviewed, 0 unreviewed.
- `ahpele_reqscan.py --register` → **83 rows, 0 not found, 0 unmatched**.
- Author's recomputation check (`check2.py`) → **0 failures, 0 warnings**: feeder ampacity/voltage drop (3 %, 2 % emergency)/40 % fill; short-circuit ratings vs recomputed fault (MSB 17.93 kA / 22 kA; worst utilisation 0.876); photometric re-run of all 36 spaces and whole-building LPD 0.2626 ≤ 0.285 W/ft²; step-load dips 10.55 % ≤ 15 % and recovery 1.44 s ≤ 3 s; register/finding sequence; cross-reference titles; no brackets, notes, blanks or metric-only units.
- Every section opens with `SECTION nn nn nn` / title / date, has literal `PART 1/2/3`, numbered articles, `a./(1)/(a)/1.` lists and ends `-- End of Section --`.

## Disposition of the independent review
All 26 findings were confirmed against the source documents and corrected in place (generator parameter schedule, 22 kA switchboard, LP2A 400 A bus, 10-ohm grounding, independent NETA Level III testing, 10-year LED warranty, 0-10 V only, exact cross-reference titles, 26 05 48/Ip = 1.5, 5-year sealed study engineer, restored full guide text, inch-pound units, sequential numbering). None was rejected; the table of dispositions, including the two remedies that differ from the reviewer's suggestion and why, is appended to `/tmp/ahpele/independent_review.md`.
